sources.title: Oodi Helsinki Central Library: Studios

sources.title: UNESCO: Sauna culture in Finland
sources.note: 2020 description: water on heated stones, home and public saunas, family transmission and multiple heating types. No health efficacy claim.

sources.title: Finlex: Original Constitution Act of Finland, 1919

sources.note: 1918 sovereignty, interrupted Danish connections in 1940, 1944 republic ceremony, buses, tents, choir and sporting displays, wind and rain.

sources.title: Odinn Melsted: Relieving the Housewife

sources.title: University of Iceland: History

sources.title: Port of Siglufjörður: Herring Era Museum

sources.note: 24 October 1975, withdrawal of paid and household work, meetings and singing, estimated crowd at Lækjartorg. Participation estimates not used as precise counts.

sources.title: Alþingi: Constitution of the Republic of Iceland, 1944

sources.title: Estonian Information System Authority: ID card turns twenty

sources.title: Estonian State Electoral Office: reports and studies on internet voting

sources.title: UNESCO: smoke sauna tradition in Võromaa

sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Ukrainization
sources.note: 1923-1933 policy; education, publishing and predominantly Ukrainian adult literacy campaign.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine: Famine of 1921-23
sources.note: Drought, war damage, requisitions and exports, hunger and relief; no unsupported single-cause attribution or precise death estimate.

sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Berezil

sources.title: ICOMOS: World Heritage potential of twentieth-century urban heritage

sources.title: Institute of History of Ukraine: Ukrainian orthography of 1928
sources.note: 1927 conference participants; 1928 approval and 1929 adoption by scholarly bodies in Soviet Ukraine and Lviv.

sources.note: PDF page 1 title and publication year 1929, page 2 approval resolution; electronic reproduction. File name 1928 denotes rules, not printed edition date.

sources.note: Referendum figures: 1 December 1991, 84.18 percent turnout, 90.32 percent of participants supported independence.

sources.note: 2024 joint Ukraine/Estonia inscription; repeated wax-resist dyeing, symbolic wishes, family transmission, birth/christening/wedding gifts. Full indexed text checked.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Finland imported from 1914 includes Russian grand-ducal years; independence 1917 and republic 1919. Iceland imported from 1900 includes Danish crown period, home rule 1904, sovereign kingdom 1918 and republic 1944. Iceland has no 1938 feature although its catalog span continues; no assumption of extinction. Finland 1914/1920/1930 bounding boxes closely match later borders while 1938 extends farther east to 32.834 E; eastern and Petsamo boundaries require upstream review, not narrative endorsement.

Separate phase narratives preserve legal state continuity while keeping interwar institutions distinct from post-1991 life. Imported Estonia ends in 1945, but occupation began in 1940. The interwar geometry must not be treated as an exact reconstruction of the 1920 Treaty of Tartu boundary.

Separate interwar and restored-republic cards describe phases of the legally continuous Latvian state. Imported 1920-1945 span is not an independence chronology; occupation began in 1940 and full independence returned in 1991. Imported snapshot bounds closely resemble later Latvia; do not present them as a verified Abrene-era border.

The 1920 Ukraine feature excludes Crimea and much western Ukraine, consistent with early Soviet Ukraine rather than a modern independent state extending to 1930. Treat boundaries as coarse snapshots amid changing control. Separate modern card begins historically in 1991, despite imported label 1994. Modern mapped territory includes Crimea and represents internationally recognized territory, not current military control.
